definition: Climate-informed siting and routing changes the location, alignment, route or deployment configuration of a project-financed investment because of identified climate or disaster hazards. Counts when the project selects, relocates or modifies a site or route to avoid or reduce exposure to flooding, erosion, landslides, extreme heat, wildfire, storms, sea-level rise or another identified hazard. The defining intervention is the location or routing decision itself; the assessment producing the evidence belongs to cra, while physical protection at the selected location belongs to resilient_infrastructure_design. The hazard rationale must be explicit and should not be inferred merely because infrastructure is located in a hazard-prone area. Does not count for ordinary network planning, expansion, land acquisition, environmental routing unrelated to climate or disaster risk, or siting discussed only as a recommendation. Prioritising or targeting the most exposed areas for investment does not count: it decides where to help, not where to avoid a hazard.
note: Do not classify hazard mapping or risk analysis here unless it results in a project siting or routing decision. Underground deployment belongs here only when the decision to place infrastructure underground is explicitly made to avoid a location-dependent hazard; physical protection of underground infrastructure belongs to resilient_infrastructure_design. v4 (2026-10-20): Dev's revision; measures are defined by the intervention, the asset map gives the asset.
